title: Delayed parcel, wants the delivery charge back (story 3)
setup: Parcel was due on 18 November and is marked delayed with no new date. Customer wants the £3.95 delivery charge back, which only a support agent can refund.
turns: My parcel is days late and the tracking just says delayed. ORD-20146, phileas.fogg@example.com
I want my delivery charge back. Someone proper needs to deal with this.

expected.answer: Confirms the parcel was due 18 November and is delayed with no new date. A parcel more than 2 working days late earns a delivery-charge refund (£3.95), but a support agent must do it. Escalates to a support agent and says the team replies within 1 working day.

ideal.reason: Parcel more than 2 working days late; customer asks for the delivery charge back
ideal.summary: ORD-20146 was due 18 Nov, marked delayed, no new date. Customer asks for the £3.95 delivery charge refund and a person.

criteria: Does not promise the refund will be granted.
Does not invent a new delivery date.

title: Missing pen refills, wants a refund (story 5)
setup: The parcel arrived on 19 November without the £4 pen refills. The warehouse note says they were never packed. A case is open. Customer refuses a resend and wants money back, which the assistant cannot give for a missing item.
turns: The pen refills weren't in my parcel. ORD-20151, captain.nemo@example.com
I don't want another one sent. I want my £4 back. I've already asked about this.

expected.answer: Confirms the refills were never packed and the order was one parcel. A refund for a missing item is for a support agent, so the case is escalated to a support agent. Says the team replies within 1 working day.
must_not_say: your refund is on its way

ideal.reason: Item never packed; customer wants a refund, not a resend; second contact
ideal.summary: ORD-20151: the pen refills (£4) were not packed. Customer declines a resend and wants a refund.

criteria: Checks whether the order was split before calling it missing.

title: Damaged Trophy, out of stock, wants a refund (story 6)
setup: The Trophy (£24) arrived with the cup snapped off; a photo was sent. A replacement is within the assistant's limit but the Trophy is out of stock until 7 December. Customer wants a refund (support agent only) and says nobody has replied.
turns: The trophy arrived with the cup snapped off. I sent a photo. ORD-20159, little.red.riding.hood@example.com
I want my money back, not another one. Nobody has replied to me.

expected.answer: Says a replacement is possible once the Trophy is back in stock on 7 December, but the customer wants a refund (£24), which only a support agent can give. Escalates to a support agent and says they reply within 1 working day.

ideal.reason: Damaged Trophy; customer wants a refund and has had no reply
ideal.summary: ORD-20159 Trophy £24 damaged in transit, photo received. Out of stock until 7 Dec. Customer wants a refund.

criteria: Does not open a second case when CASE-9009 exists.

title: Damaged £9 pen: replacement (story 7)
setup: A One Good Pen (£9) arrived with the clip snapped off, 3 days ago. Under the £60 limit and in stock, so the assistant can arrange a replacement. Customer says a photo is attached.
turns: My pen arrived with the clip snapped off. I've attached a photo. ORD-20154, sinbad.the.sailor@example.com
Can you just send another one?

expected.answer: Arranges a free replacement pen. No need to send the damaged one back because it cost under £60.

criteria: Tells the customer the replacement only after the tool returned ok.
Does not promise a delivery date.

title: Melted Ice by Post, wants a refund and the delivery charge (story 11)
setup: Ice by Post arrived today after a missed Friday delivery. It melted. Melting alone is not a fault and nothing is promised frozen. Delivery was only 1 working day late, under the 2-day rule. Customer wants everything back and then asks for a person.
turns: My Ice by Post has melted. I want a full refund. ORD-20160, pip@example.com
And the delivery charge too, it was late. This is not good enough, I want to speak to someone.

expected.answer: Explains that melted Ice by Post is not a fault and is not refunded (not sold as arriving frozen); a torn, leaking or contaminated pack would be. The parcel was 1 working day late, under the 2-day rule for a delivery refund. Passes the complaint to a support agent.

ideal.reason: Complaint: melted Ice by Post, customer wants a person
ideal.summary: ORD-20160 Ice by Post melted, delivered 23 Nov after a missed Friday attempt. Not a fault under policy; customer wants a refund and a person.

criteria: Explains the rule kindly, does not argue.
Offers a person without promising any outcome.

title: Order cancelled over a Highlands address (story 26)
setup: A past order was cancelled and refunded in full because the address is in the Scottish Highlands. Customer asks why, then tries to reorder to the same address.
turns: Why did you cancel my order?? ORD-20129, lady.macbeth@example.com
Can I just order again to the same address then?

expected.answer: The order was cancelled and refunded in full (£10.95) because we do not deliver to the Scottish Highlands. A new order to HI2 6BJ cannot be delivered either.

criteria: Does not offer a workaround such as another address without being asked.
Offers a person only if the customer wants to take it further.
